claim: 73 TFs in human K562 cells were characterized for spacing relationships based on ChIP-seq data.
source: We characterized spacing relationships for 73 TFs of K562 cells covering diverse TF families (Hu et al., 2019) based on the ChIP-seq data from ENCODE data portal (Davis et al., 2018).
evidence: The manuscript explicitly states the number of TFs analyzed and the cell type used.

claim: 42% of ChIP-seq peaks on average contain at least one binding site of the corresponding TF.
source: 42% of peaks on average contain at least one binding site of corresponding TF (Supplementary file 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the analysis of ChIP-seq data.

claim: 45 of the 73 TFs examined exclusively exhibited relaxed spacing relationships with other TFs.
source: By dissecting each TF's binding sites based on their spacing relationships with co-binding TFs, we found that 45 of the 73 TFs examined exclusively exhibited relaxed spacing relationships with other TFs (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a direct result from the computational analysis shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Twenty-five factors could participate in either relaxed or constrained interactions, depending on the specific co-binding TFs.
source: Twenty-five factors could participate in either relaxed or constrained interactions, depending on the specific co-binding TFs.
evidence: This is a direct statement from the results section describing TF spacing patterns.

claim: Only three TFs interacted with only constrained spacing.
source: Only three TFs interacted with only constrained spacing, some of which might show additional relaxed spacing relationships by expanding the current set of TFs.
evidence: This is a direct result from the spacing analysis.

claim: Among 29 TF pairs with constrained spacing relationships, most bind closely to each other within 15 bp spacing.
source: Among 29 TF pairs with constrained spacing relationships, most bind closely to each other within 15 bp spacing (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the data shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: GATA1-TAL1 and NFATC3-FOSL1 recognize composite motifs.
source: Some of these TF pairs have been reported to recognize composite motifs such as GATA1-TAL1 and NFATC3-FOSL1 (Macián et al., 2001; Ng et al., 2014; Figure 1D; Figure 1—figure supplement 3)
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous literature and data shown in figures.

claim: MEF2A-JUND and CEBPB-TEAD4 are novel constrained spacing patterns discovered by this analysis.
source: some are novel constrained spacing patterns discovered by our analysis such as MEF2A-JUND and CEBPB-TEAD4 (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a new finding from the current study's analysis.

claim: TFs exhibiting relaxed spacing show progressively declining frequency of co-binding with distance from the center of the reference TF.
source: TFs exhibiting relaxed spacing are exemplified by ETV1-TAL1 and JUND-KLF16, in which the frequency of co-binding progressively declines with distance from the center of the reference TF (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is an observation from the spacing distribution data shown in Figure 1D.

claim: The same type of spacing relationship is usually observed in different motif orientations.
source: In addition, the same type of spacing relationship is usually observed in different motif orientations (Figure 1D), consistent with previous findings (Lis and Walther, 2016).
evidence: This observation is supported by data in Figure 1D and previous literature.

claim: The same TF pairs can have similar spacing relationships in different cell types, exemplified by CEBPB and JUND in K562 and HepG2 cells.
source: The same TF pairs can have similar spacing relationships in different cell types, exemplified by CEBPB and JUND in K562 and HepG2 cells (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a comparative observation across cell types shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: Binding activities quantified by ChIP-seq tags were indifferent at various spacings for both constrained and relaxed TF pairs.
source: Despite more frequent binding events occurring at specific spacings for constrained TF pairs or at closer spacings for relaxed TF pairs, the binding activities quantified by ChIP-seq tags were indifferent at various spacings, suggesting that the spacing preference is not a determinant of TF binding activity (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is an observation from the ChIP-seq tag analysis shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: Most relaxed spacing relationships remain regardless of repetitive or nonrepetitive regions.
source: As a result, most of the relaxed spacing relationships remained regardless of repetitive or nonrepetitive regions (Figure 1—figure supplement 6).
evidence: This is a result from the analysis comparing repetitive and nonrepetitive regions.

claim: Some constrained TF pairs showed constrained spacing only in repetitive regions and not in nonrepetitive regions.
source: Some constrained TF pairs, however, showed constrained spacing only in repetitive regions and not in nonrepetitive regions (Figure 1—source data 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the region-specific analysis.

claim: EGR1 and JUND exhibited a constrained spacing at 29 bp specifically in SINEs.
source: For example, EGR1 and JUND exhibited a constrained spacing at 29 bp (Figure 1D), but this relationship is observed specifically in SINEs (Figure 1—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a specific observation from the data shown in the figures.

claim: InDels between TF binding sites have similar sizes compared to those at binding sites and those in background regions, the majority of which are less than 5 bp.
source: We found that InDels between TF binding sites have similar sizes compared to those at binding sites and those in background regions, the majority of which are less than 5 bp (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the InDel size distribution analysis.

claim: Most of the InDels are singletons or rare variants.
source: Most of the InDels are singletons or rare variants (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Figure 2—source data 1).
evidence: This is a result from the allele frequency analysis of InDels.

claim: Singletons were significantly more enriched between the binding sites of TFs with constrained spacing.
source: On the contrary, singletons were significantly more enriched between the binding sites of TFs with constrained spacing, whereas high-frequency variants were significantly more depleted between these binding sites.
evidence: This is a statistical result from the enrichment analysis.

claim: High-frequency variants were significantly more depleted between binding sites of TFs with constrained spacing.
source: On the contrary, singletons were significantly more enriched between the binding sites of TFs with constrained spacing, whereas high-frequency variants were significantly more depleted between these binding sites.
evidence: This is a statistical result from the enrichment analysis.

claim: InDels between TF binding sites with constrained spacing could be just as damaging as those at binding sites.
source: Since common variants are associated with less deleteriousness and rare variants with more deleteriousness (Lek et al., 2016), these findings suggest that InDels between TF binding sites with constrained spacing could be just as damaging as those at binding sites, whereas InDels between TF binding sites with relaxed spacing might have a much weaker effect.
evidence: This is an inference based on the enrichment patterns and established knowledge about variant deleteriousness.

claim: InDels between TF binding sites with relaxed spacing might have a much weaker effect than those at binding sites.
source: Since common variants are associated with less deleteriousness and rare variants with more deleteriousness (Lek et al., 2016), these findings suggest that InDels between TF binding sites with constrained spacing could be just as damaging as those at binding sites, whereas InDels between TF binding sites with relaxed spacing might have a much weaker effect.
evidence: This is an inference based on the enrichment patterns and established knowledge about variant deleteriousness.

claim: PU.1 and C/EBPβ follow a relaxed spacing relationship independent of their motif orientations.
source: Based on our computational framework for characterizing spacing relationships (Figure 1A), these two TFs follow a relaxed spacing relationship independent of their motif orientations (Figure 3A; KS p-value < 1e-6).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis with statistical significance.

claim: Both PU.1 and C/EBPβ binding activities quantified by ChIP-seq tags were indifferent at various spacings.
source: Moreover, both PU.1 and C/EBPβ binding activities quantified by the ChIP-seq tags were indifferent at various spacings (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is an observation from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Most of the natural InDels are less than 5 bp similar to those found in the human population.
source: Most of the natural InDels are less than 5 bp similar to those found in the human population (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a comparative observation of InDel size distributions.

claim: PU.1 binding is most strongly affected by PU.1 motif mutation, followed by C/EBPβ motif mutation and other motif mutation.
source: All the four independent comparisons showed that PU.1 binding is most strongly affected by PU.1 motif mutation, followed by C/EBPβ motif mutation and other motif mutation.
evidence: This is a result from the effect size analysis across multiple strain comparisons.

claim: Spacing alterations have a smaller effect size on PU.1 binding than any motif mutations.
source: Spacing alterations have a smaller effect size than any of these motif mutations, but still a relatively larger effect than variants affecting neither binding affinity nor spacing.
evidence: This is a comparative result from the effect size analysis.

claim: The effect of spacing alterations on PU.1 binding was independent of the size or direction of InDels.
source: Despite the moderate effect size of spacing alterations, we found such effect was independent of the size or direction of InDels (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is an observation from the correlation analysis shown in Figure 3D.

claim: Changes of PU.1 ChIP-seq tags are strongly correlated with changes of binding affinity measured by changes of PWM scores.
source: On the contrary, changes of PU.1 ChIP-seq tags are strongly correlated with changes of binding affinity measured by changes of PWM scores (Figure 3D).
evidence: This is a correlation result shown in Figure 3D.

claim: The effects of motif mutation and spacing alteration are not varied by the initial spacing between PU.1 and C/EBPβ motifs.
source: In addition, the effects of motif mutation and spacing alteration are not varied by the initial spacing between PU.1 and C/EBPβ motifs (Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: Similar findings for spacing tolerance were observed in C/EBPβ binding, except that C/EBPβ motif mutation had the largest effect size.
source: Similar findings were observed in C/EBPβ binding, except that C/EBPβ motif mutation had the largest effect size and the strongest correlation with C/EBPβ binding activity as expected (Figure 3E and F; Figure 3—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a comparative result from the C/EBPβ binding analysis.

claim: Consistent relationships were observed in promoters and enhancers despite most informative genetic variants being located at enhancers.
source: Despite that most of the informative genetic variants are located at enhancers and relatively few within promoters, we saw consistent relationships in promoters and enhancers (Figure 3—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an observation from the region-specific analysis.

claim: A relaxed spacing relationship exists between PU.1 and p65 and between c-Jun and p65.
source: We observed a relaxed spacing relationship between PU.1 and p65 and between c-Jun and p65 (Figure 3—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is a result from the spacing analysis of these TF pairs.

claim: InDels altering motif spacing had a much smaller effect size on TF binding than motif mutations for PU.1-p65 and c-Jun-p65 pairs.
source: In addition, InDels altering motif spacing had a much smaller effect size on TF binding than motif mutations (Figure 3—figure supplement 6), consistent with our findings from PU.1 and C/EBPβ.
evidence: This is a comparative result from the effect size analysis.

claim: Altered spacing demonstrated weaker effects on nascent transcription than motif mutations.
source: Like for TF binding, altered spacing demonstrated weaker effects on nascent transcription than motif mutations (Figure 3G), which is consistent with the significant correlations between changes in TF binding and changes in the level of nascent transcripts (Figure 3—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is a result from the GRO-seq analysis.

claim: There is a weak correlation between changes in GRO-seq tags and the size of InDels, in contrast with a much stronger correlation with changes in binding affinity.
source: The relative tolerance of spacing alteration was further supported by a weak correlation between changes in GRO-seq tags and the size of InDels, in contrast with a much stronger correlation with changes in binding affinity (Figure 3H).
evidence: This is a correlation result from the GRO-seq analysis.

claim: Similar relationships were observed for effects of InDels on local acetylation of histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27ac).
source: Similar relationships were observed for effects of InDels on local acetylation of histone H3 lysine 27 (H3K27ac) (Figure 3—figure supplement 7; Figure 3—figure supplement 8), which provides an alternative surrogate for enhancer and promoter activity (Creyghton et al., 2010).
evidence: This is a result from the H3K27ac ChIP-seq analysis with citation to previous work.

claim: ERG is an ETS factor that functions as an LDTF in endothelial cells that selects poised enhancers where p65 binds in a hierarchical manner upon interleukin-1β (IL-1β) stimulation.
source: ERG is an ETS factor that functions as an LDTF in endothelial cells that selects poised enhancers where p65 binds in a hierarchical manner upon interleukin-1β (IL-1β) stimulation (Hogan et al., 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: ERG and p65 follow a relaxed spacing relationship.
source: ERG and p65 follow a relaxed spacing relationship according to our method (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a result from the computational analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Only a small portion of bQTLs and hQTLs directly mutates an ERG or p65 motif.
source: As a result, only a small portion of bQTLs and hQTLs directly mutates an ERG or p65 motif (Figure 4B; Figure 4—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the QTL classification analysis.

claim: Motif mutations are enriched in bQTLs compared to non-QTLs.
source: However, such motif mutations are enriched in bQTLs compared to non-QTLs (Fisher's exact p < 1e-4).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the enrichment analysis.

claim: InDels that alter motif spacing are significantly depleted in p65 bQTLs.
source: On the contrary, InDels that alter motif spacing are significantly depleted in p65 bQTLs (Fisher's exact p = 1.3e-15).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the enrichment analysis.

claim: InDels from the dozens of individuals are predominantly shorter than 5 bp by following a similar size distribution of those in human populations.
source: These InDels from the dozens of individuals are predominantly shorter than 5 bp by following a similar size distribution of those in human populations (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is a comparative observation of InDel size distributions.

claim: Variants that mutate both ERG and p65 motifs have the strongest effects on both p65 binding and histone acetylation in IL-1β-treated endothelial cells.
source: Despite being the minority among QTLs, variants that mutate both ERG and p65 motifs have the strongest effects on both p65 binding and histone acetylation in IL-1β-treated endothelial cells (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is a result from the effect size comparison shown in Figure 4C.

claim: ERG binding and the basal level of histone acetylation are significantly affected by ERG motif mutations in untreated endothelial cells and not by p65 motif mutations.
source: In comparison, ERG binding and the basal level of histone acetylation are significantly affected by ERG motif mutations in untreated endothelial cells and not by p65 motif mutations, consistent with the hierarchical interaction of p65 only upon IL-1β stimulation (Figure 4—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a result from the effect size analysis in untreated cells.

claim: In both conditions of endothelial cells, spacing alterations have the smaller effect size than motif mutation categories and are not significantly different from likely non-functional variants in the 'other' group.
source: In both conditions of endothelial cells, spacing alterations have the smaller effect size than motif mutation categories and are not significantly different from likely non-functional variants in the 'other' group.
evidence: This is a comparative result from the effect size analysis.

claim: The CRISPR/Cas9 system generated a wide range of InDels with most deletions being <30 bp and short insertions usually less than 5 bp.
source: Based on the bioinformatic analysis of the ultra-deep sequencing reads from the input DNA samples, we saw that the CRISPR/Cas9 system generated a wide range of InDels with most deletions being <30 bp and short insertions usually less than 5 bp (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a quantitative observation from the sequencing data analysis.

claim: The CRISPR/Cas9 system provides longer deletions than natural genetic variations found across mouse strains and in human populations.
source: It provides longer deletions than natural genetic variations found across mouse strains (Figure 3—figure supplement 1) and in human populations (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a comparative observation of InDel size distributions.

claim: InDels altering spacing have significantly weaker effects on C/EBPβ binding in comparison to those overlapping with at least one of the binding sites.
source: We found that InDels altering spacing have significantly weaker effects on C/EBPβ binding in comparison to those overlapping with at least one of the binding sites (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a statistical result from the CRISPR experiment analysis.

claim: For some test regions, the effects of pure spacing alterations are almost negligible, exemplified by test region #6 and test region #1.
source: For some test regions, the effects of pure spacing alterations are almost negligible, exemplified by test region #6 (Figure 5D and E) and test region #1 (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is an observation from the CRISPR experiment results.

claim: Test region #6 is located near a highly expressed gene Prdx1 and has strong binding of PU.1 and C/EBPβ binding and strong signals of H3K27ac and chromatin accessibility indicated by ATAC-seq in ER-Hoxb8 cells.
source: Test region #6 is located near a highly expressed gene Prdx1 and has strong binding of PU.1 and C/EBPβ binding and strong signals of H3K27ac and chromatin accessibility indicated by ATAC-seq in ER-Hoxb8 cells, which all support its potential regulatory function (Figure 5D).
evidence: This is a descriptive observation from multiple data types shown in Figure 5D.

claim: At test region #6, spacing alterations ranging from 5 bp increase to 22 bp decrease did not have a strong effect on TF binding.
source: In general, spacing alterations ranging from 5 bp increase to 22 bp decrease did not have a strong effect on TF binding, indicated by a log2 odds ratio close to 0 (Figure 5E).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the CRISPR experiment shown in Figure 5E.

claim: Deletions overlapping with the TF binding sites resulted in a general decrease in TF binding activity.
source: On the contrary, deletions overlapping with the TF binding sites resulted in a general decrease in TF binding activity.
evidence: This is an observation from the CRISPR experiment results.

claim: The Ly9 enhancer (test region #1) has a 5 bp insertion between PU.1 and C/EBPβ binding sites in BALB, NOD, and PWK mice, and shows unaffected binding of PU.1 and C/EBPβ in the BMDMs of these strains.
source: This Ly9 enhancer also has a 5 bp insertion between PU.1 and C/EBPβ binding sites in BALB, NOD, and PWK mice, and shows unaffected binding of PU.1 and C/EBPβ in the BMDMs of these strains (Figure 5—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is an observation from the natural genetic variation analysis.

claim: At test region #1, C/EBPβ binding activity was generally unaffected by spacing alterations only, whereas deletions overlapping TF binding sites substantially diminished TF binding.
source: As a result of the synthetic InDels, the C/EBPβ binding activity was generally unaffected by spacing alterations only, whereas deletions overlapping TF binding sites substantially diminished TF binding (Figure 5—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a result from the CRISPR experiment at test region #1.

claim: PU.1 binding showed general tolerance of synthetic spacing alterations in contrast with significantly weaker PU.1 binding resulted from motif alterations.
source: We further measured PU.1 binding using ChIP-seq at three out of six test regions and saw general tolerance of synthetic spacing alterations in contrast with significantly weaker PU.1 binding resulted from motif alterations (Figure 5—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a result from the PU.1 ChIP-seq analysis of CRISPR-edited regions.

claim: Relaxed spacing relationships were the dominant pattern of interaction for majority of the 73 co-binding TFs analyzed.
source: By classifying the genome-wide spacing relationships of 73 co-binding TFs as 'constrained' or 'relaxed', we revealed that relaxed spacing relationships were the dominant pattern of interaction for majority of these factors.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main finding from the spacing analysis.

claim: Approximately half of the TFs could also participate in constrained spacing relationships with specific TF partners.
source: Among these factors, approximately half could also participate in constrained spacing relationships with specific TF partners.
evidence: This is a summary statement from the spacing analysis results.

claim: The study confirmed TF pairs known to exhibit constrained relationships (e.g., GATA1-TAL1).
source: We confirmed TF pairs known to exhibit constrained relationships (e.g., GATA1-TAL1) and identified previously unreported constrained relationships for additional pairs, including EGR1 and JUND.
evidence: This is a summary of findings that includes both validation of known relationships and discovery of new ones.

claim: The study identified previously unreported constrained relationships for additional pairs, including EGR1 and JUND.
source: We confirmed TF pairs known to exhibit constrained relationships (e.g., GATA1-TAL1) and identified previously unreported constrained relationships for additional pairs, including EGR1 and JUND.
evidence: This is a new finding from the current study.

claim: The finding of a subset of constrained TF interactions on a genome-wide level is consistent with locus-specific examples provided by functional and structural studies of the interferon-β enhanceosome and in vivo studies of synthetically modified enhancer elements in Ciona.
source: Overall, this finding of a subset of constrained TF interactions on a genome-wide level is consistent with the locus-specific examples provided by functional and structural studies of the interferon-β enhanceosome (Panne, 2008) and in vivo studies of synthetically modified enhancer elements in Ciona (Farley et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings with previous literature.

claim: Direct protein-protein interactions are observed between bound TFs at the interferon-β enhanceosome, analogous to interactions defined for cooperative TFs that form ternary complexes.
source: Direct protein-protein interactions are observed between bound TFs at the interferon-β enhanceosome, analogous to interactions defined for cooperative TFs that form ternary complexes (Morgunova and Taipale, 2017; Reményi et al., 2003).
evidence: This is established knowledge cited from previous literature.

claim: The spacing analyses in this study did not directly consider the possible overlap between TF binding sites.
source: However, unlike the previous in vitro study that identified over 300 TF-TF interactions (Jolma et al., 2015), the spacing analyses in our study did not directly consider the possible overlap between TF binding sites.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study's methodology.

claim: The study is not able to discover constrained TFs that recognize overlapping motifs or distinguish effects of spacing alterations from effects of InDels on overlapping composite motifs.
source: Thus, we are not able to discover constrained TFs that recognize overlapping motifs or distinguish effects of spacing alterations from effects of InDels on overlapping composite motifs.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of the current study.

claim: The findings based on ChIP-seq data were consistent with recent in vivo profiling of TF co-occupancy on single DNA molecules, which discovered a lack of association between TF co-occupancy and precise spacing or orientation of motifs.
source: Our findings based on ChIP-seq data were consistent with the recent in vivo profiling of TF co-occupancy on single DNA molecules, which discovered a lack of association between TF co-occupancy and precise spacing or orientation of motifs (Sönmezer et al., 2021).
evidence: This is a comparison of the current findings with recent literature.

claim: The observation that most TF pairs exhibited relaxed spacing relationships has intriguing implications for the mechanisms by which functional enhancers and promoters are selected from chromatinized DNA.
source: The observation that most TF pairs exhibited relaxed spacing relationships has intriguing implications for the mechanisms by which functional enhancers and promoters are selected from chromatinized DNA.
evidence: This is an interpretive statement about the implications of the findings.

claim: Relaxed spacing relationships appear to not require specific protein-protein interactions between TFs for collaborative binding at most genomic locations.
source: In contrast to ternary complexes of TFs that cooperatively bind to composite elements as a unit, relaxed spacing relationships appear to not require specific protein-protein interactions between TFs for collaborative binding at most genomic locations.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed spacing patterns.

claim: The basis for collaborative binding interactions between TFs with relaxed spacing remains poorly understood.
source: Although pioneering TFs necessary for selection of cell-specific enhancers have been reported to recognize their motifs within the context of nucleosomal DNA (Zaret and Carroll, 2011), the basis for collaborative binding interactions between TFs with relaxed spacing remains poorly understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the current state of knowledge in the field.

claim: The current studies relying on natural genetic variation and mutagenesis experiments concluded clear tolerance of spacing alterations between binding sites of TFs with relaxed spacings.
source: While the current studies relying on natural genetic variation and mutagenesis experiments concluded clear tolerance of spacing alterations between binding sites of TFs with relaxed spacings, the extent to which this set of binding sites is representative of all regulatory elements is unclear.
evidence: This is a summary statement of the main conclusion with acknowledgment of limitations.

claim: The proportion of outliers with significant differences in TF binding between mouse strains associated with InDels occurring between TF binding sites was generally similar to that observed at genomic regions lacking such InDels.
source: However, the proportion of outliers was generally similar to that observed at genomic regions lacking such InDels, and such strain differences may be driven by distal effects of genetic variation on interacting enhancer or promoter regions (Hoeksema et al., 2021; Link et al., 2018a).
evidence: This is an observation from the analysis with citation to previous work.

claim: The remarkable tolerance of synthetic InDels at two independent endogenous genomic locations between PU.1 and C/EBPβ binding sites strongly support the generality of relaxed binding interactions for these two proteins.
source: The remarkable tolerance of synthetic InDels at two independent endogenous genomic locations between PU.1 and C/EBPβ binding sites strongly support the generality of relaxed binding interactions for these two proteins.
evidence: This is an interpretive statement about the significance of the CRISPR experiment results.

claim: While the densities of C/EBP binding sites increase with decreasing distance to PU.1 binding sites over a 100 bp range, deletions from 1 to >30 bp between PU.1-C/EBPβ pairs did not result in improved binding.
source: Intriguingly, while the densities of C/EBP binding sites increase with decreasing distance to PU.1 binding sites over a 100 bp range (Figure 3A), deletions from 1 to >30 bp between PU.1-C/EBPβ pairs did not result in improved binding.
evidence: This is an observation from the CRISPR experiment results compared to the spacing distribution.

claim: Relatively constant binding was observed with progressive deletions bringing two binding sites close together until the deletions started to cause mutations in one or both motifs.
source: Instead, relatively constant binding was observed with progressive deletions bringing two binding sites close together until the deletions started to cause mutations in one or both motifs.
evidence: This is an observation from the CRISPR experiment results.

claim: The lack of requirement for exact spacing and remarkable tolerance of spacing alterations by TFs with relaxed spacing could potentially associate with the high turnover of TF binding sites found by previous studies.
source: The lack of requirement for exact spacing and remarkable tolerance of spacing alterations by TFs with relaxed spacing could potentially associate with the high turnover of TF binding sites found by previous studies (Vierstra et al., 2014), although further investigation would be needed to establish this association.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential implications with acknowledgment that further work is needed.

claim: A limitation of the study is that few and relatively short insertions were obtained, preventing conclusions as to the extent to which increases in spacing are tolerated.
source: A limitation of our studies is that few and relatively short insertions were obtained, preventing conclusions as to the extent to which increases in spacing are tolerated.
evidence: This is an explicit statement about a limitation of the study.

claim: The present studies provide a basis for estimation of the potential phenotypic consequences of naturally occurring InDels in non-coding regions of the genome.
source: In concert, the present studies provide a basis for estimation of the potential phenotypic consequences of naturally occurring InDels in non-coding regions of the genome.
evidence: This is a summary statement about the implications of the study.

claim: The majority of naturally occurring InDels are less than 5 bp in length.
source: The majority of naturally occurring InDels are less than 5 bp in length.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the InDel size distribution analyses.

claim: In nearly all cases, InDels of less than 5 bp size range between binding sites for TFs that have relaxed binding relationships are unlikely to alter TF binding and function.
source: In nearly all cases, InDels of this size range between binding sites for TFs that have relaxed binding relationships are unlikely to alter TF binding and function, and InDels of much greater length are frequently tolerated.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the combined results from natural variation and CRISPR experiments.

claim: InDels of much greater length than 5 bp are frequently tolerated between binding sites for TFs that have relaxed binding relationships.
source: In nearly all cases, InDels of this size range between binding sites for TFs that have relaxed binding relationships are unlikely to alter TF binding and function, and InDels of much greater length are frequently tolerated.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the CRISPR experiment results.

claim: InDels between binding sites for TFs that have constrained binding relationships have the potential to result in biological consequences.
source: In contrast, InDels between binding sites for TFs that have constrained binding relationships have the potential to result in biological consequences.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the enrichment analysis of InDels in human populations.

claim: Application of these findings to the interpretation of non-coding InDels that are associated with disease risk will require knowledge of the relevant cell type in which the InDel exerts its phenotypic effect and the types of TF interactions driving the selection and function of the affected regulatory elements.
source: Application of these findings to the interpretation of non-coding InDels that are associated with disease risk will require knowledge of the relevant cell type in which the InDel exerts its phenotypic effect and the types of TF interactions driving the selection and function of the affected regulatory elements.
evidence: This is a statement about the requirements for applying the findings to disease contexts.
